title: Context Contract
description: The contract every node that calls a model declares, per call. Origen: 19.1 (the eight design questions and the Pydantic model of src/core/context_contracts.py). It is not aesthetic documentation: it is a security interface. Criterion for use: knowledge/patterns/context-contract.md.

node.description: The node this contract governs. One call, one contract.

objective.description: What this call must decide or produce.

allowed_state_keys.description: Allow-list of state, memory or RAG fragments the call may see. An allow-list, never a deny-list: the next key added must not be visible by default.

forbidden_patterns.description: Second barrier: patterns that must never enter the call. This is GDPR minimization implemented (16.4). Optional in the schema because the allow-list is the first barrier; skill isa-context-contract refuses a contract that declares allowed data and no forbidden data.

visible_tools.description: Capabilities offered to this call, and nothing else. May be empty: a triage node offers none.

output_schema.description: The schema that validates the response, or null when the output is free text.

max_input_tokens.description: Hard input limit. An unset limit is an unlimited limit.

fallback.description: What happens when the call fails. Origen: 19.1, Literal of the Pydantic model.
